title: Implement the workspace invitation accept/redeem endpoint
acceptance_criteria: An invited user can redeem a valid scoped invite token to gain the granted workspace membership; redemption is single-use, expiry- and revocation-aware, tenant/workspace-scoped, and atomic (the WorkspaceMember is created and the invitation marked Accepted in one transaction); an invalid, expired, revoked or already-redeemed token grants nothing (fail-closed).
required_tests: Integration: a pending token redeems to exactly one WorkspaceMember carrying the invited role; a second redemption of the same token is rejected (single-use); an expired or revoked token is rejected; a token presented for the wrong workspace/tenant is hidden-404; the redeemed member can then act per their role (e.g. create a scene) end-to-end over HTTP.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (workspace membership is currently UNREACHABLE via the public API - surfaced by hands-on testing 2026-06-15: a workspace creator is not auto-membered and the only way to gain membership is a direct DB seed). The domain is already built and unit-tested: WorkspaceInvitation.Redeem()/MatchesToken()/IsRedeemable() (WorkspaceInvitation.cs ~315-358), but CORE-WS-004 shipped only the invite half with NO acceptance route (WorkspaceEndpoints.cs ~40, IWorkspaceInvitationRepository.cs ~46). Add the redeem route (e.g. POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/invitations/accept taking the plaintext token, or a token-scoped POST /api/v1/invitations/{token}/accept). Resolve the invitation by token hash within (org, workspace), verify IsRedeemable, then Redeem() + create the WorkspaceMember with the invitation role and append an audit record - all in one CORE-CONC-002 transaction. The caller is the authenticated invitee (the email is data not auth; the OIDC subject becomes the member). Fail-closed; a bad/expired/foreign token is an indistinguishable rejection (T6). Add the route to csv/api_routes.csv and docs/08; reuse WorkspaceInvitationRepository + WorkspaceMemberRepository. Pairs with CORE-WS-007/008.

title: Implement the workspace invitation revoke endpoint
acceptance_criteria: An Owner/Admin can revoke a pending workspace invitation so its token can never be redeemed; revoking an already-accepted or already-revoked invitation is rejected; revocation is tenant/workspace-scoped and audited.
required_tests: Integration: a revoked invitation no longer redeems (with CORE-WS-006); only Owner/Admin may revoke (403 otherwise); revoking an accepted invitation is rejected; a foreign-tenant or unknown invitation is hidden-404.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (an invite cannot be taken back today - the T6 revocation control is unreachable). WorkspaceInvitation.Revoke() (WorkspaceInvitation.cs ~363-380) exists with no route. Add DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/invitations/{invitationId} (or a .../revoke action). Owner/Admin only, mirroring the member-invite authorization (WorkspaceEndpoints.cs ~638-645). Reuse WorkspaceInvitationRepository; append an audit record. Fail-closed; hidden-404. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08. Depends on the invitation model; pairs with CORE-WS-006.

title: Implement the pending-invitations read endpoint
acceptance_criteria: An Owner/Admin can list a workspace's pending invitations through a PII-safe projection (invited email is the only personal datum and the token hash is never returned); results are tenant/workspace-scoped; non-privileged roles and foreign tenants are denied.
required_tests: Integration: Owner/Admin lists pending invites; a non-privileged role is 403; a foreign tenant is hidden-404; the response never contains the token hash (T6/T7).
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (manage-members has no way to see outstanding invites). Add GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/invitations returning pending invitations (id, invited email, role, status, expiry) and never the token hash. Reuse WorkspaceInvitationRepository (add a ListPendingByWorkspace query if absent) and the existing WorkspaceEndpoints Owner/Admin authorization. Fail-closed; hidden-404. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08. Pairs with CORE-WS-006/007.

title: Implement the scene reorder endpoint
acceptance_criteria: A host can move a scene to a new position within its workspace; the workspace scene ordering re-packs deterministically with no gaps or duplicates; reordering is authorized and tenant/workspace-scoped; concurrent reorders do not corrupt the order.
required_tests: Integration: reordering a scene yields the expected (scene_order, id) sequence; an out-of-range or foreign scene is hidden-404; a non-authoring role is 403; two concurrent reorders converge without duplicate orders (with CORE-CONC-006).
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (scenes can only be appended-to-end and re-packed on delete; there is no explicit user-driven reorder). Program.cs ~354-355 names the reorder route as a later story and csv/api_routes.csv has no reorder route (only GET list, POST create, DELETE, GET by-id). Add e.g. POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/scenes/{sceneId}/reorder (or a PUT with a target index). Reuse the CORE-SCENE-001 (scene_order, id) ordering and the delete-repack logic; assign order server-side (no client-trusted absolute order). Authorize Host/CoHost/Owner/Admin exactly like scene create (SceneEndpoints.cs ~360-366). Benefits from CORE-CONC-006 (Scene.Reorder is a real read-modify-write). Fail-closed; hidden-404. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08.

title: Emit or formally prune the unemitted session events
acceptance_criteria: Every event in csv/event_catalog.csv is either actually emitted by a Core command or explicitly removed from the catalog (or marked deferred with a named owner), so the catalog is a contract not aspirational; the spec-consistency check validates the emitted set against the non-deferred catalog.
required_tests: Integration: each newly-emitted event (e.g. SessionCreated on session create, SceneCreated on scene create, ContentBlockCreated on content-block create, RecapGenerated on recap generation) persists and reaches its documented recipients with identifier-only payloads (no PII, T7); a spec-consistency test fails if the catalog lists a non-deferred event that no command emits.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (spec-integrity; the session-event analogue of CORE-SPEC-002, which made the entitlement/store catalog real). docs/24 'Genuinely deferred items' records that 7 catalog events are documented but unemitted: the emitted set is the 8 names in apps/api/Realtime/SessionEventTypes.cs (SessionStarted/Ended, ParticipantJoined/Left, SceneActivated, VisibilityRuleChanged, ContentRevealed/Hidden) while csv/event_catalog.csv and docs/09 list 15 - the extra 7 are SessionCreated, SceneCreated, ContentBlockCreated, PrivateMessageSent, AssetRevealed, SessionNoteCreated, RecapGenerated. Decide per event: EMIT the ones tied to an existing Core command (SessionCreated on POST .../sessions, SceneCreated on scene create, ContentBlockCreated on content-block create, RecapGenerated on the recap worker job) via the existing ISessionEventPublisher + SessionEventRecipientResolver, payload identifier-only (T7), inside the CORE-CONC-002 transaction; PRUNE or explicitly defer with a named owner the vertical/future ones (PrivateMessageSent, AssetRevealed, SessionNoteCreated). Then extend scripts/spec-consistency.ps1 to check the emitted set vs the non-deferred catalog (CORE-SPEC-001 checks docs/09 vs csv only, never emission). Update csv/event_catalog.csv, docs/09, docs/24. Reuse SessionEventTypes + the publisher; never widen an audience (subject-gated events stay gated).

title: Consolidate inline role checks into a single capability policy
acceptance_criteria: Per-action authorization is expressed once as a role-to-capability mapping (the documented authorization matrix) and consumed by every endpoint, replacing the duplicated inline exact-role checks; behavior is unchanged (the same roles are allowed/denied) and csv/authorization_matrix.csv is the single source of truth.
required_tests: Unit: the capability policy returns the authorization-matrix decision for each (role, action); a regression suite proves every migrated endpoint allows/denies exactly the roles it did before; an undefined role is denied (fail-closed).
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (maintainability/correctness hardening; no behavior change). The role-to-capability mapping is repeatedly named a later story (the workspace authorization policy): WorkspaceMember.cs ~232, OrganizationMember.cs ~181, TenantContext.cs ~31, IOrganizationMemberRepository.cs ~45 - yet authorization is implemented as duplicated inline exact-role checks scattered across the endpoints (e.g. HasRole(Owner) || HasRole(Admin) in Workspace/Scene/Content/Session/Asset handlers), which can drift independently of csv/authorization_matrix.csv. Introduce a single capability policy driven by the matrix (the same source CORE-SPEC-001 validates) and route every endpoint decision through it, keeping the exact non-linear set-membership semantics (never a >/< ordering). CORE-WS-005 covers the policy TESTS but not the consolidated engine. Pure refactor + tests; reuse MembershipRole + the matrix. No contract or route change.

title: Record the deliberately-absent capabilities as explicit dated deferrals
acceptance_criteria: Each capability that exists in the model but is deliberately not exposed (export/recap read endpoints, entity / entity-type / template create and list endpoints, preview-as-participant) and each known spec contradiction is recorded as an explicit dated deferral or decision naming its owner (Core-later vs vertical) and rationale, so a reader can tell an intentional omission from a gap.
required_tests: Doc/CSV consistency stays green (the CORE-SPEC-001 checks); no Core source change.
notes: TIER 4 LOW (hygiene; docs/csv only, no new endpoints). Consolidate the many are later stories and are deliberately not built/wired here markers into one explicit deferral register (extend docs/24 'Genuinely deferred items' or add a docs section), annotating each as Core-deferred or vertical-owned with a rationale, mirroring how CORE-DOC-002 and CORE-DR-004 formalized deferrals: (a) the deliberately-absent read/CRUD endpoints - Program.cs ~358/401/423/445/482/500/710/1304, ExportManifestProjection.cs ~146 and ExportJob.cs ~239 (no export read/download route), Recap.cs ~32-55 (no recap read route), the Entity/EntityType/Template/Visibility explicit-ids contract notes, ContentBlockEndpoints.cs ~41; CORE-E2E-003 already records recap/export have no HTTP read endpoints by design. (b) Reconcile the active-scene contradiction: Program.cs ~354 says a session activates a scene through its active scene pointer in a later story, but SessionEventTypes.cs ~63 states revealing a scene IS the scene switch (no separate active-scene command) - decide whether an explicit active-scene pointer is a real future feature or reveal-is-activation is the final contract, and record the decision. (c) Note the session-participant roster deferral (docs/11 ~55; SessionEventRecipientResolver.cs ~54) is a deliberate design (correctness held by session-keyed groups + the session-scoped gate), not a gap. This only makes the deferrals auditable; it adds no endpoints. Pairs with CORE-SPEC-001/CORE-EVT-004.
